text: Panning refers to the process of distributing a sound signal, whether originally monaural or stereophonic, into a new stereo or multi-channel sound field. This distribution is determined by a pan control setting. A common interface for this control is a pan pot, short for "panoramic potentiometer," which functions as an analog knob or slider. Physical recording consoles often feature these pan controls, typically positioned with a range from 8 o'clock (fully left) to 4 o'clock (fully right). In audio mixing software, virtual versions of these pan pots appear as on-screen knobs or sliders, providing the same functionality.
title: Panning (audio)

text: Panning is an audio technique employed in mixers to manipulate the stereo image. One specific application involves using panning to transform a stereo signal into a mono signal. This occurs when the left and right channels of a stereo source are panned centrally, meaning they are sent equally to both the left and right output channels of the mixer.
title: Panning (audio)

text: In a market economy, decisions concerning the production of goods and services are fundamentally guided by the interaction of supply and demand, establishing market prices. A key characteristic is that the allocation of resources for production is primarily determined by capital and financial markets. This contrasts sharply with planned economies, where state-controlled entities make investment and production choices.
title: Market economy

text: The mammalian sperm cell is structured with distinct parts: the head, neck, midpiece, and tail. The head encompasses the nucleus, which holds the densely coiled chromatin fibres, and is anteriorly covered by an acrosome containing enzymes for egg penetration. The neck section includes the sperm centriole. The midpiece features a central filamentous core encircled by numerous mitochondria, which are vital for generating ATP to power the sperm's journey through the female reproductive tract. The tail, or flagellum, is responsible for the lashing movements that drive the spermatocyte forward.
title: Sperm

text: Motile sperm cells, equipped with a single flagellum, propel forward uniquely and cannot swim backwards. Their movement towards an egg requires a water medium. Spermatozoa rely on mitochondria for energy, specifically those containing fructose within the seminal fluid. These mitochondria are situated in the midpiece, which is positioned at the base of the sperm head.
title: Sperm

text: An equilateral triangle is defined by having all three sides of equal length. This specific property contributes significantly to its symmetry. It possesses three distinct lines of reflection symmetry, meaning it can be folded onto itself along three different axes.
title: Equilateral triangle

text: Sharecropping is an agricultural arrangement where a farmer uses a portion of another person's land and gives a share of the produced crops to the landowner, keeping the remainder for themselves. This practice has a long history and exists in various forms across different cultures and agreements. Some systems are based on tradition, while others are formalized by law. Specific legal contract systems include the Italian mezzadria, the French métayage, the Spanish mediero, and the Islamic muqasat.
title: Sharecropping

text: Athens rose to prominence as the wealthiest Greek city-state around the late 6th century BCE. This ascent was significantly aided by the discovery of rich silver veins in the nearby mountains, which substantially increased their wealth. The city also developed an efficient trading network with other Greek states, focusing heavily on pottery, which constituted a large portion of their exports. Furthermore, Athens began importing grain because its own soil was not particularly fertile.
title: Economic history of Greece and the Greek world

text: The Canadian Prime Minister serves at Her Majesty's pleasure, meaning the post does not have a fixed term. Once appointed and sworn in by the governor general, the prime minister remains in office until he or she resigns, is dismissed, or dies. However, the term of a majority government is limited by an amendment to the Canada Elections Act, which came into effect in 2007. This amendment restricts the government's time in office to four years, setting the election day as the third Monday in October of the fourth calendar year following the previous polling date.
title: Prime Minister of Canada

text: A microscope slide is a fundamental component in preparing samples for observation. It is typically used in conjunction with a cover slip, a smaller glass sheet placed over the specimen on the slide. To position the slide correctly for viewing, it is placed **on the microscope's stage**. This placement allows for its secure holding, often achieved through specialized slide clips or clamps. In certain advanced or hygienic settings, a cross-table mechanism might be employed for precise, automated movement of the slide **on the microscope's stage**, ensuring accuracy without manual contact.
title: Microscope slide

text: The Articles of Confederation, formally the Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union, served as the first constitution for the United States of America, establishing a loose alliance of the thirteen original states. Approved by the Second Continental Congress in 1777 and fully ratified by the states by 1781, it created a federal government intended only to possess the powers the colonies had previously granted to the king and parliament. A core principle of this agreement was to safeguard the independence and sovereignty of the states, meaning they retained the vast majority of governmental authority. Therefore, under the Articles of Confederation, the states held significantly more power than the central government.
title: Articles of Confederation

text: The history of Hawaii starts with human settlements sometime between 124 and 800 CE. Around 1200, Tahitians specifically arrived and initiated the settlement of the islands, laying the foundation for the Hawaiian civilization that followed. This initial arrival marked the beginning of a period of isolation lasting another 500 years.
title: History of Hawaii

text: Born on November 2, 1944, Michael Buffer is an American ring announcer known for boxing and professional wrestling. Buffer is also noted for his habit of rolling certain letters and adding inflections when pronouncing fighters' names. text: Product/market fit is a concept defined by Mark Andreessen. He stated that it occurs when a company is operating within a favorable market and has developed a product capable of fulfilling the needs of that market. Some interpretations also involve creating a minimum viable product to address existing problems or needs.
title: Product/market fit

text: Kidney transplantation is the surgical transfer of a healthy kidney from one person (the donor) to another (the recipient) suffering from end-stage renal disease. This procedure relies on organs sourced either from deceased donors or, crucially, from living-donor transplantation.
title: Kidney transplantation

It delves into contemporary social topics like sexuality, safe sex, promiscuity, and femininity, often contrasting friendships with romantic entanglements. title: Sex and the City

title: Golden State Warriors

text: Early in the twentieth century, specifically during its first half, John B. Watson established methodological behaviorism. His approach fundamentally rejected introspective methods, instead proposing that behavior should be studied solely through the measurement of observable actions and events. While Watson focused on the stimulus-response mechanisms seen in classical conditioning, notably those investigated by Ivan Pavlov, his work defined the initial phase of behaviorist thought. It was later, in the 1930s, that B. F. Skinner would introduce his own influential philosophy, radical behaviorism, which expanded the scope to include private events like thoughts and feelings.
title: Behaviorism

text: The idea of a North American Union, modeled after the European Union, has been discussed since the mid-19th century. This concept involves the potential integration of Canada, Mexico, and the United States. Following the implementation of NAFTA and the Maastricht Treaty, there was increased speculation about the possibility of forming such a union. While some proposals suggested a full-fledged union like the EU, others advocated for less extensive integration, such as a customs union or common market, among Canada, Mexico, and the US.
title: North American Union

text: The Ranjit Sagar Dam, also known as the Thein Dam, is a significant hydroelectric project located in the Indian state of Punjab. It was constructed by the Government of Punjab specifically on the Ravi River, a major waterway that forms a border between the states of India's Punjab and Jammu and Kashmir. Shah pur Kandi Township is the site for this dam, which is also situated near the cities of Pathankot and Kathua. Notably, 60% of the reservoir it forms is situated in Jammu and Kashmir. This facility represents the largest hydroelectric dam within Punjab. Development commenced with feasibility studies in 1953, followed by geotechnical investigations until 1980. Actual construction started in 1981, with the generators becoming operational in 2000 and the entire project completed by March 2001.
title: Ranjit Sagar Dam

text: In J. R. R. Tolkien's legendarium, the Undying Lands, a title sometimes used for Valinor, refer to the realm of the Valar located in Aman. While the name implies eternal life, the land itself did not grant immortality to mortals, though only non-immortals were permitted to reside there under specific circumstances. These exceptions included the surviving bearers of the One Ring—Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, and Samwise Gamgee—and possibly Gimli son of Glóin, who accompanied his friend Legolas to Valinor.
title: Valinor

text: The Undying Lands, once accessible to Men after the destruction of the Númenorean kingdom of Númenor, are now distant and veiled. However, for the Elves, these islands remain reachable only through a specific means: the ancient, straight road across the sea, and by utilizing ships that possess the unique power to sail beyond the normal confines of the world, past the spheres of the earth itself. Valinor, the blessed land on these islands, is the ultimate destination reserved for them.
title: Valinor

text: Felix Baumgartner, an Austrian skydiver and BASE jumper born on April 20, 1969, achieved significant fame for his jump from a helium balloon at high altitude on October 14, 2012. This event established world records for the highest skydive, estimated at 39 km, and the fastest recorded skydive speed, approximately 1,357.64 km/h or Mach 1.25. He notably became the first individual to break the sound barrier during a non-vehicular descent from the stratosphere. These texts represent a distinct category within the Christian Old Testament, specifically excluding certain books and passages not present in the original Hebrew Bible. Their canonical status and classification as separate from the protocanonical books (those in the Hebrew canon) and apocryphal books (non-canonical but sometimes considered edifying) were definitively established through the actions of the Council of Trent. This significant council concluded its deliberations and issued its definitive canon list in the year **1546**, thereby formally designating the deuterocanonical collection.
title: Deuterocanonical books

text: In plant anatomy, sieve tube elements, also referred to as sieve tube members, are highly specialized elongated cells found in the phloem tissue of flowering plants. These cells are connected to one another at their ends, forming a continuous sieve tube structure. The primary role of this sieve tube is the transport of carbohydrates, mainly sucrose, throughout the plant, for instance, from leaves to fruits and roots. It's important to note that unlike xylem vessel elements which mature into dead cells specialized for water conduction, sieve elements remain living. A unique characteristic is that these cells lack a nucleus once they reach maturity.
title: Sieve tube element

text: The Second Battle of El Alamein, occurring between October 23 and November 11, 1942, was a pivotal engagement in the Western Desert Campaign of the Second World War. It took place near the Egyptian railway halt known as El Alamein, cementing its location within Egypt. This battle served as the turning point for the conflict, following the earlier First Battle of El Alamein, which had successfully halted the Axis forces' advance into Egypt. Lieutenant-General Sir Bernard Law Montgomery assumed command of the Allied Eighth Army in August 1942, after the dismissal of General Claude Auchinleck and the unfortunate death of his temporary replacement, Lieutenant-General William Gott.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: The Panzerarmee Afrika, led by Generalfeldmarschall Erwin Rommel, achieved a significant advance into Egypt by July 12th, 1942, following their victory at Gazala. This push threatened the British Empire's control over the Suez Canal and the region of Mandatory Palestine. Consequently, the British Eighth Army was forced to withdraw to a position near the coast, specifically within 80 kilometers of Alexandria, and the defense line was established around El Alamein. This location proved crucial as it was situated near the Qattara Depression, which restricted the front the Axis forces could exploit and prevented tanks from maneuvering into the area. The Axis advance was finally halted at this very point in early July, marking the start of the First Battle of El Alamein.
title: Second Battle of El Alamein

text: American foreign policy after the start of World War I was initially neutrality. President Woodrow Wilson, who had shown little interest in foreign affairs before 1913, declared this stance upon the outbreak of hostilities in 1914. Working to broker peace, the administration insisted on its neutral rights, which included allowing private corporations and banks to loan money to either side. While the British blockade effectively prevented loans to Germany, the sinking of the RMS Lusitania by a German U-boat in 1915, killing 128 American civilians, significantly shifted public opinion against Germany. Despite support from various groups, Wilson maintained neutrality throughout the early years of the conflict, even denouncing violations by both sides. This policy continued until Wilson requested a declaration of war in April 1917.
title: History of U.S. foreign policy
